title: Energy systems working together

draft.title: Energy systems working together
card: The three energy systems do not switch on and off one at a time. All three are working at any moment, but they do not supply equal amounts.
The intensity of the activity and how long it lasts decide which system supplies most of the energy.
A very short, all-out effort draws mostly on the ATP-PC system. A hard effort lasting up to a couple of minutes draws mostly on anaerobic glycolysis.
A long, steady effort draws mostly on the aerobic system. When the intensity or length of the activity changes, the main supplier changes too.
draft.remember: All three systems work at once. Intensity and length decide which one does most of the work.

a.q: Which statement best describes how the energy systems work during exercise?
opts: All three work at once, and one supplies the most
Only one works at a time, then the next takes over
The aerobic system stops while the others are working
The system with the most energy works alone
a.why: All three systems contribute at any moment, and the activity decides which one supplies most. The idea that they take turns is tempting, but the card says they do not switch on and off one at a time.
a.clue: Think about whether any system ever fully stops.

b.q: Priya jogs at a steady pace for 40 minutes, then sprints hard for the last 5 seconds. Which system supplies most of the energy for the sprint?
opts: None, as the aerobic system stays on
b.why: A very short, all-out effort draws mostly on the ATP-PC system. The aerobic system supplied most of the energy for the jog, but the change in intensity and length changes the main supplier. It does not stop working.
b.clue: Look at how long and how hard the sprint is, not the jog before it.

a.best: All three work at once, and one supplies the most
